To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) The performance of the analog least mean square loop for self-interference cancellation in in-band full duplex OFDM systems is determined by the windowing function rather the pulse shaping; (ii) OFDM signals lead the error of the channel modelling with the analog filter to be reduced, which provides a much higher interference cancellation.
the performance of analog least mean square loop for self-interference cancellation in in-band full duplex OFDM systems is primarily dependent on windowing function.

1) The ALMS loop is a good candidate for IBFD OFDM systems because the ALMS loop can provide a much higher level interference suppression compared to the case of single carrier systems; 2) The ALMS filter performance is mainly determined by the windowing function; and 3) The OFDM system is a good candidate to be used in IBFD systems due to the fact that the error of the adaptive filter is reduced in OFDM systems.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of an analog least-mean-square (ALMS) filter for the purpose of self-interference (SI)-cancellation in full-duplex systems.
a new method to improve the performance of ALMS loop in IBFD OFDM systems.
the performance of the analog LMS (ALMS) adaptive filter employed for SI suppression in in-band full duplex (IBFD) OFDM systems.

the performance of an ALMS loop for OFDM systems is better than that in a single carrier system.
the ALMS filter is more suitable for IBFD OFDM systems than IBFD single carrier systems.

the ALMS filter is a good choice for SI cancellation in IBFD OFDM systems, especially when the number of sub-carriers is large.
